title: ANOVA as a named partition of squares
dek: Wikipedia ANOVA is SS_between / SS_within. It is an LRT/F-test costume in Gaussian linear models, not a separate religion.
story: ANOVA on Wikipedia is the partition of total sums of squares into between-group and within-group pieces, referred to an F. In a Gaussian linear model this is the same nesting as an LRT (up to the usual σ² story).
stats-lrt is the likelihood language. wiki-doe and stats-factorial own design. This card is the encyclopedia name people search after a lab meeting says 'just run ANOVA'.
Non-Gaussian outcomes (binary DST, counts) do not become Gaussian because you typed aov().
deep: One-way, two-way, repeated measures are design statements. The software word ANOVA does not tell you the design.
Type I/II/III SS fights are order-of-entry fights in unbalanced data — not a Wikipedia religious war you should import unexamined.
Kruskal–Wallis is a rank cousin, not 'nonparametric ANOVA' with the same null.
TB example: MIC by lineage as a factor is an ANOVA only if you believe the Gaussian linear model.

visual.caption: ANOVA's reduced model is intercept-only (or additive); the full model adds factors. The F is a Gaussian costume of a nested comparison.
